related_resources.reason: Key Takeaways; Ostinato/Ground Bass/Chaconne distinction; Multiple Harmonizations; Purcell case. Does not establish properties of lecture-original scores.
ABACA as one Classical rondo type, contrasting refrain/couplets; full chapter not inspected.
Refrains, contrasting episodes, common ABACA design, variation and tonal context in Classical repertory. Historical scope; not a universal structural prescription.
Five-part A-B-A-C-A layout and possible ornamented/abbreviated returns.
Author-hosted chapter pp.1-4: recurring thematic content and formal functions are not equivalent; describes Caplin's own theoretical position, not a consensus theorem.
Abstract distinguishes acoustic, notated and perceived repetition, and perceptual roles; not evidence our examples work for particular listeners.
Abstract supports repeated material as organizing attention in time; no observed listener trials for the classroom pieces.
Publisher confirms essay attribution and original date. Text itself also inspected from university-hosted teaching scan.
Printed pp.9-11 explicit distinction between compositional procedures and perceptible musical processes; this lecture does not claim its through-development example is Reich-style process music.
Abstract identifies scholarly disagreement on the theoretical definition of developing variation. Do not overextend to score classification.
Defines through-composed in terms of composing new music for successive stanzas or sections without repeating, useful historical context.
Synchronized track exports and processor-application option; does not describe or validate this Python score renderer.

claim_evidence.anchor: Here are four notes: E, G, A, G.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original shared motif; first bar of all three pieces is E4,G4,A4,G4, dur=1.
claim_evidence.source_locator: examples/comparing-forms-041000.json: reference_motif and all pieces lead bar 1

claim_evidence.anchor: The first moves upward by three semitones, the second rises by two, and the third falls by two.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: MIDI intervals 64 to 67 (+3), 67 to 69 (+2), 69 to 67 (-2). Not an external experimental finding.

claim_evidence.anchor: Each occupies forty bars of four-quarter meter at one hundred beats per minute.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Identical tempo, meter, and 40-bar length in each original piece.

claim_evidence.anchor: All use the same schematic synthesizer voices: an upper lead, a lower bass, and an inner supporting voice.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: The three pieces share exact waveform/gain/pan configs for these three voices. Ardour reference only contextual.

claim_evidence.anchor: A ground bass repeats a bass line while other music changes over it.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Gotham Key Takeaways and main Ground Bass definition.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Gotham, Ground Bass: Key Takeaways and first two paragraphs

claim_evidence.anchor: An ostinato is a repeated pattern; a ground bass is the particular case in which that repetition belongs to the bass.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Definitions distinguished in Gotham chapter.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Gotham, Ground Bass: terminological distinction below Key Takeaways

claim_evidence.anchor: Historically, composers also used ground bass as the basis of chaconnes and passacaglias, but those labels carry additional conventions.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Gotham identifies chaconne/passacaglia as subgenres, including triple-meter conventions in Baroque cases.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Gotham, Ground Bass: paragraph beginning It is easy to confuse

claim_evidence.anchor: In the opening bar, the bass plays C followed by G.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original score bar 1, bass C3 at beat0 dur2 G3 at beat2 dur2.

claim_evidence.anchor: In the second, A followed by E.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original score bar 2 bass A2,E3.

claim_evidence.anchor: In the third, F followed by C.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original score bar 3 bass F2,C3.

claim_evidence.anchor: In the fourth, G followed by D.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original score bar 4 bass G2,D3.

claim_evidence.anchor: It does this ten times without changing its pitches or its timing.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Exact cross-cycle 4bar ground bass event signatures are asserted by local validator.

claim_evidence.anchor: Bars five through eight preserve the bass literally, while the melody holds some notes longer and shortens others.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Ground cycle index 1 varies melodic durations only.

claim_evidence.anchor: Bars nine through twelve subdivide the melody into more attacks, making the upper surface busier.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Ground cycle index 2 has 6 lead events per bar instead of 4.

claim_evidence.anchor: Bars thirteen through sixteen move the lead down an octave.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: All four original melody pitches lowered 12 semitones in ground cycle 4.

claim_evidence.anchor: Bars twenty-five through twenty-eight delay several lead attacks
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Half-beat rests precede the lead attacks at every bar of this cycle.

claim_evidence.anchor: Bars twenty-nine through thirty-two leave deliberate spaces
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Each bar of this cycle omits a beat of melodic events and begins with a held note.

claim_evidence.anchor: Elizabeth Hellmuth Margulis's research examines how repetition can establish expectations and redirect attention.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Margulis abstract distinguishes repetition modes and attentional orientation; expectation is a broad pedagogical paraphrase rather than a measured effect for our pieces.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Margulis 2018 abstract; On Repeat ch3 abstract pp55-74

claim_evidence.anchor: Repeating the bass does not mean repeating one fully specified harmony.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Gotham demonstrates ground bass re-harmonization; a bass pitch does not specify full harmonic realization.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Gotham, Ground Bass: Multiple Harmonizations of a Given Bass

claim_evidence.anchor: In Gotham's analysis of Purcell, changing harmony and imitative relationships are part of how repetition supports variety.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Chapter sections Harmony, Imitation, Rhythm and Meter on Purcell Sonata in G Minor Z 807.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Gotham, Ground Bass: Analysis Purcells Sonata in G Minor

claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Bar 40 lead ends C5, bass G2 then D3. This is not verified as a stylistic perfect authentic cadence.

claim_evidence.anchor: The form of our work is A, B, A, C, A.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: ABACA structural designation is a common Classical five-part rondo scheme; specific composition is original.

claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original B first bar has B4,D5,E5,F#5,E5 lead events.

claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Validator compares time-relative lead pitch/duration signatures A1 and A2.

claim_evidence.evidence_detail: The second A bass uses durations 3+1 vs first A 2+2. External form theory is background only.

claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original C begins A4 2 beats, C5 1.5 beats, B4 0.5; bass A2 and E3; minor color is interpretive.

claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original lead bar8 C5 dur3 G4 dur1; bar40 C5 dur4.

claim_evidence.anchor: Recognizing a repeated tune tells us something important, but it does not by itself explain what the tune is doing at each appearance.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Caplin chapter pp1-4 argues thematic content and formal function distinct; not a formal proof about this new composition.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Caplin, Formal Function versus Thematic Content, printed pp1-4

claim_evidence.anchor: The third composition begins E, G, A, G as before.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Continuous piece bar1 exactly reference melody.

claim_evidence.anchor: Our study is instrumental. It has recognizable regions of growth and relaxation
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Original work contains only synthetic instrumental voices. Through-composed background distinguishes text-based term, not proof of a specific formal label.

claim_evidence.anchor: By bar seven, an inner voice begins to enter
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Continuous inner events absent bars1..6, enter bar7.

claim_evidence.anchor: From roughly bar fifteen through bar twenty-nine, the upper surface becomes busier.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Lead event density varies in middle; the writing intentionally qualifies this as roughly, not monotonically every bar.

claim_evidence.anchor: At bar forty, the lead settles on a single C for the complete measure, over a bass that begins on C.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Lead C4 at bar40 dur4, bass C3 dur3 then G3 dur1. The tonic bass only begins the bar; narration no longer implies it lasts the entire measure.

claim_evidence.anchor: Steve Reich, in his 1968 essay *Music as a Gradual Process*, describes musical processes that determine the sound-to-sound details and overall form together
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Primary essay printed p9 explicitly contrasts compositional process with pieces that are literally processes.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Reich 1968, Music as a Gradual Process p9; OUP 2004 pp34-36

claim_evidence.anchor: Our third study is not that.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: This original score uses chosen transformations/sectional interventions; does not result solely from one autonomous audible process.

claim_evidence.anchor: Jack Boss's survey of the concept stresses that analysts have disagreed about its definition.

claim_evidence.anchor: In the score, no complete eight-bar lead window is duplicated elsewhere.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Exact time-relative event signatures for all 33 consecutive 8-bar lead spans are pairwise distinct; not evidence of listener-perceived uniqueness.

claim_evidence.anchor: All three works share the same opening four notes, length, meter, and basic synthesizer setup.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: All three piece JSONs have shared lead bar1, 40bars, 100bpm, same voice configurations.

claim_evidence.anchor: The distinction is not between repetitive and non-repetitive music.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Narration synthesis: all three involve lower-level recurrence; not a literature claim that all music must repeat.

claim_evidence.anchor: A model can be told to use call-and-response, or to avoid it.

claim_evidence.evidence_detail: CLI --anonymous shuffles names deterministically and writes answer_key.json. No double-blind claim.

evidence_scope_note: Mechanical anchoring validates exact passages, URLs and score invariants, not historical authenticity or perceptual preferences. Sources with publisher_abstract_only access are explicitly marked.
description: Develops one four-note motif into three contrasting musical forms—a repeating ground, a rondo, and continuous development—to compare how structure changes a listener’s expectations.
